\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]\footnotesize\raggedright
\item \textit{Notes:} Panel A reports means in bp for the 38-household persistence sample, weighting each purchase equally. The alpha charge equals 20 times recent alpha plus the compounding remainder. Panel B regresses factor-only returns on 20 times recent alpha, both in bp. Both panels use unwinsorized returns, charges, and predictors. The all-purchase regression covers 232 of the 233 households with trade-date purchases, as the remaining household has no purchase with both an estimable benchmark and complete 20-day returns. Purchase regressions include fixed effects for 20-day entry blocks. Standard errors in these regressions and in Panel A are clustered by household and entry block. For the fixed-date sample of stocks traded by congressional households during the study period, I average cross-sectional slopes over 139 dates spaced 20 trading days apart and use a three-lag Newey--West standard error. Intervals are 95\%, and tests of $\lambda=1$ are two-sided. See Appendix~\ref{app:continuation} for alternative transformations and size subsets and Appendix~\ref{app:continuation-placebos} for comparisons of return levels at actual and shifted dates.
\end{tablenotes}\end{threeparttable}
